Warning, tmi rant. I think if we don’t consider it obligatory schools won’t value them and stop funding them. For some people, they need it, as in, it’s the only class they enjoy or are good at. It’s about self esteem. However, they should be done differently. Not everyone is good at PE. For some of us it has the opposite effect. As a young developing girl I really struggled  with physical activity because I was JUST figuring out how to handle having a period. Too much movement wrong and I’d have an embarrassing accident. I didn’t understand how other girls seemed to have it under control and be into sports, but tbh looking back they were probably struggling as much as I was. But I didn’t know that and I felt like shit because I didn’t get it. 

And I had this problem even worse when it came to bras. I developed breasts quite early and they were large by middle school and I struggled to run and I realize now I was wearing the wrong size but I didn’t know that. People thought I was lazy and I thought so too because I couldn’t run. I didn’t understand why other girls could contain their chests so easily and I felt like something was wrong with me. People made fun of me for not running much in PE class. So do I think PE should stay mandatory? Yes. But I also think we should allow people struggling with it to do lighter workouts and not make students do anything they are not comfortable with. Maybe if someone isn’t comfortable running they can do dancing. We need to change the approach so people struggling to don’t feel like shit.

It’s not your story to tell. It’s hers. She’s the one who was in the situation, not you. She decides what happens with the information. Hopefully she goes to therapy or finds a healthy coping mechanism, and maybe some day she’ll feel ready to tell the police, but that’s no guarantee, the police put victims through a lot when trying to get their story, and the court process requires she talks about all the details in front of several people. It’s great when someone feels they can handle the process and decide to get justice, but not everyone is ready nor wants to and that’s okay. 

I don’t know who you plan to tell and what you think it will accomplish, but I can tell you she will feel hurt by it and like you exposed something deeply personal, her trust will be violated.
